title: Inult and Riska
text: “That’s right. Heroes aren’t everything. The problem is…”

My Father trailed off. With the slave hunts intensifying, the opportunity to use this passage never arose. It’s not that there’s no way to use it even now, but I think the issues surrounding the slave hunts will be resolved to some extent once the Queen returns. Well, there is the issue that—since I asked my Father not to act like a saint—a situation like the loop where he stayed in Melromarc might not happen again.
“Even if we spread the word by word of mouth, that would end up luring not just slave hunters but the country’s soldiers as well… I hope it goes well even if we limit it to Demi-Humans and Beastmen.”
“It’ll be fine, Naofumi-san… You just need to kill all those guys as you go.”
Somehow, Itsuki’s choice of words feels rather extreme. Is his sense of justice running amok? He doesn’t seem to be showing any remorse.
“So, does this mean you’ve achieved your objective, Naofumi-san?”
“I suppose so, Eclair. Shion, it seems the secret left behind by the late lord was something like this.”
“Hmm… It’s not entirely useless…”
“That’s… true.”

It wasn’t a complete waste of effort, but it’s not exactly a place with much practical value. That’s true. Back when I was being deceived by Crimson Swine, if my Father had encountered the moles who were still safe here during the kidnapping of my Finacée, this passageway might have come in handy. …It might be a good idea to put it to use in future loops. After all, it was built with good intentions. Let’s keep that in mind.
“I guess it’s our turn next? Itsuki… um, well, how did you end up looking like that? And why are we even here? Wait… could it be… there was talk about a Beastman killing a noble inside Melromarc…”
“There’s no need to hide anything or lie right here. Yes, I killed him. That scoundrel.”
Itsuki replied with an eerie laugh, his voice laced with anger.
“O-oh, I see. Looks like a lot’s been going on.”
My father, clearly overwhelmed, replied, almost at a loss for words.
“Before I explain the details—”
“Ah, wait, Itsuki. Ren’s with me right now. It’ll save us some trouble if we call him over before we talk. Itsuki might have information that Ren wants to know.”
“Is Ren actually here with Naofumi? That would definitely save us some trouble. Still… I was hoping to meet up with Naofumi and the others soon, but I never expected to run into them here.”

For some reason, Itsuki muttered that he was glad they’d met before things got serious. I wonder what he was planning to do? And the Mole that Itsuki brought along seems to be looking at him with a slightly exasperated expression.
“Emia. I’ve made up my mind—I won’t back down, even if it’s you.”
“Yes… I understand.”
It seems Itsuki is paying the mole quite a bit of attention. And Riska—aka the “stalker pig”—appears to be following Itsuki around, looking a bit frightened.
“Um… you’re the missing noble’s child… right?”
“Bub, bubbub.”
“Ah, yeah. That’s right.”
Riska is speaking Pig-speak. I don’t really get it. So I’ll ask Yuki-chan to translate.
“Yuki-chan, Yuki-chan. What on earth is this one saying?”
“She’s saying, ‘That’s right. I’m the maid who’s been following Lord Itsuki because I saw something… Since he saved me, I’m helping out as things have turned out.’”
It seems this situation is different from the loops we’ve experienced so far. What does “I saw it” mean? Is it because she’s a maid?

“So, Rishia, since you’ve met Naofumi and the others, if you promise not to talk about our situation, you’re free to go home. I’ve come to understand your character well enough during our journey so far. Even if it was just how things turned out, I’m sorry for the trouble I’ve caused you.”
“Bub! Bubbuh! Bu”
“She’s saying, ‘No way! Itsuki-sama, I haven’t had any trouble at all! Please let me help you!’”
Hmm, even if the circumstances are a little different, Riska still wants to stay with Itsuki.
“Well then, Itsuki… um, shall we go? I’m thinking of using my Portal Skill to return.”

“Even with Naofumi and the others, there’s still a chance—albeit small—that they might use the portal to kick us out. If anything happens, we’ll escape through the portal instantly. If you try to trick us, we’ll make sure to get our revenge, so be prepared.”
Itsuki seems a bit wary. This suspicious nature reminds me of my Father from the first world.
“I wouldn’t do something like that. That said… since there’s a bounty on Itsuki and the others, maybe we should hide our faces and appearances as much as possible…”
“By the way, should we point that out?”
For some reason, Éclair is pointing at me. What is she looking at? I turned around, but there’s nothing there.
“Nah, no need to worry about it. After all, the others haven’t noticed it either, have they?”
What on earth are they talking about? Starting with the moles, everyone’s glancing this way from time to time.
“Hmm? A hair accessory?”
“I guess so?”
“Yuki’s going to copy that, too.”
And with that, Yuki-chan is for some reason sticking a fallen twig in her hair like a hairpin. Anyway, thanks to Father’s suggestion, we were able to return to the circus.
“Ah, welcome back, Mr. Iwatani.”
“Vo, Vofu.”

The Rabbit Man and Wolf both looked at me before immediately shifting their gaze back to Father. I’m not quite sure why, but he muttered later that he couldn’t keep up if he reacted to every little thing.
“I’m back. Could you go get Ren for a moment? I need to talk to him about something important, and let’s head to the back so no one sees us.”
With that, my father led Itsuki and Mole—whom he’d been hiding under his cloak—into the tent. They entered while using their stealth skills to hide their forms, of course. Riska is with Éclair.
“Our outing’s over…”
“Let’s go play with everyone over there!”
“Yay!”
Filo-tan went off to play with Kou.
“Ah, you’re back.”

For some reason, Ren reacted just like the rabbit men did; he turned toward Father, then looked surprised. Itsuki dashed out from under his Father’s cloak and ran over to Ren, and the two stared at each other. Slowly, their gazes met on the Santa hat perched atop Ren’s head.
“That appearance… it’s really you, Ren, right?”
“Could it be… Itsuki?”
“Yes, Ren—what’s going on with you, too?!”
“Ah!”
And just like that, Ren and Itsuki looked at each other as if a sense of camaraderie had suddenly blossomed between them.
“I see. So that’s why you understood right away.”
“I suppose so.”
“Naofumi, why was Itsuki the one sent to investigate Eclair and the others?”
“Ah, about that…”
Father explained the whole situation to Ren.

“So it was a secret escape route out of the country that a noble—who died during the wave while mediating relations with the Demi-Humans and Beastmen—had been hiding, and for some reason, Itsuki was accompanying the guard there.”
“Yeah. So, Itsuki… how on earth did that situation even happen? I was under the impression we were working with our comrades…”

“Ah, when I turned into this form, Itsuki went to talk to you before heading to Naofumi’s place. But when I did, they yelled at me, saying, ‘There’s no way Itsuki would develop symptoms like that. Don’t be fooled!’ and refused to even listen to what I had to say.”
As Ren explained this, Itsuki raised his eyebrows with a look of displeasure, then tilted his head and glared at him with anger in his eyes.
“I see… So they’re pulling off such a underhanded cover-up? They really are a foolish bunch.”
